Contributing to aciR

Source: CONTRIBUTING.md

Contributions are welcome. This document says what the package expects, so that a contribution is not turned away for a reason it could not have known.

Reporting a problem

Open an issue at https://github.com/biometryhub/ACI/issues. A numerical report is most useful with the model specification, dt, mu0, R0, the output of summary() on the result, and sessionInfo(). If the metric looks wrong, say what you expected and why. For this package that is usually the most informative part of the report.

The one rule that is not negotiable

The oracle tests are a release gate. They run the package’s own filter, smoother and metric against fixtures generated by an independent MATLAB harness and must reproduce them to 1e-6. They never skip. A change that breaks them is wrong until proven otherwise, and “the test is too strict” is not a proof. The observed agreement is at 4.6e-14, so a change that pushes it to 1e-6 has altered the numerics by eight orders of magnitude.

Fixtures are never regenerated to make a test pass. See the refresh policy in inst/extdata/oracle-manifest.yml.

Adding a validated capability

New numerical capability needs an oracle before it needs an implementation. That oracle must be something the contributor did not also author: the authors’ reference implementation, an analytic solution, an established package, or a published table. A test whose expected values came from running the new code is a record of what the code did, not a check that it is right.

If no independent oracle is available, say so in the pull request. An explicit [unverified] is a contribution; a green test that grades nothing is a liability.

State what your oracle covers and what it does not. The package learned this the hard way: the dyad fixture pins the noise cross-covariance at zero, so it executes the terms carrying it without ever grading them, and a 99.6%-coverage figure said nothing about that gap.

Style

R code follows the package’s committed .lintr. Two points that trip people up:

  • The numerical core uses the notation of the method paper (L_x, S_xoS_x, A_j and relatives) rather than R naming convention. This is deliberate, the correspondence to the published equations is what makes the code auditable, and the .lintr admits those names by a narrow rule. Do not rename them, and do not widen the rule to cover new ones without saying why.
  • Validation goes in a named .aci_check_* helper in R/aci-validate.R, not inline in the function body. Errors use stop(..., call. = FALSE) and name the offending argument and index.

Run devtools::test() and lintr::lint_package() before opening a pull request. Error messages are locked by snapshot tests; if you change one deliberately, update the snapshot in the same commit.

Documentation

Documentation is roxygen-generated. Run devtools::document() and commit the generated man/ files. If a change affects what the package claims about its own evidence, it affects inst/extdata/oracle-manifest.yml and the Validation and the independent oracle vignette too.

Code of conduct

By contributing you agree to abide by the Code of Conduct.
